main_text.l: partes sunt, sed quatenus organicæ, & in-
strumentales, aut mistam edunt actionem.
Id autem, quòd postea Fernelius producit
ex Galeni sententia, & authoritate, nimirum
partis substantiam ad robur non parū con-
ferre, nō satis probat materiam per se non-
nullis subijci morbis, forma salua & tempe
ramento. Nam hoc loco substantia pro ma-
teria sumi, non est verisimile, quandoqui-
dem per se nihil agit materia, sed est dunta
xat passionis causa. Immaterialia enim ni-
hil pati queunt. At id robur efflagitat, quòd
agendi uim habet. Quare substantia hic su-
mitur pro corpore similaris partis, quod
quidem edit actionem. Quamuis etiam ad
partis similaris substantiam robur pertine-
at, ipsum tamen à solo temperamento pro-
ficisci testantur Hippocrates, Galenus, &
cæteri præclariores medici. Adde quòd o-
mnis partium similarium imbecillitas, quæ
robori opponitur, ab aliqua intemperie sem-
per prouenit, quemadmodum iam ostendi-
mus. Quod ibidem his subiungit Ferneli-
us, nempe spiritus, carnis, & solidarum par-
tium substantiam esse materiam, ex qua quæ-
libet similaris pars nostri corporis est con-
flata: à veterum dogmate omnino alienum
videtur.

page.notes: Transcription is a faithful reading of the printed text, with the long s normalised to s and the u/v and i/j spelling adjusted. Some words are uncertain and should be checked against the scan: "dunta" (line about "est dunta xat passionis") is probably a printing error for "duntaxat"; I have kept it as printed. The phrase "quæ robori" and "substantia hic sumitur" are clear. The printed "Quod ibidem his subiungit" and "nempe spiritus" are read as printed. Some letters near the ink-damaged edges, especially in "intemperie" and "est verisimile", should be verified. Marginal notes: none printed on this page. The reference mark "y" is not present. Printing errors left as printed: "dunta", "semper prouenit", and the words "partes sunt" are as they appear. Text below the column: none.
